diagnostic_evidence.quote: Furthermore, the sub-level sets $f^{-1}((-\infty, a])=\{ \param\in \Param\,:\, f(\param)\le a \}$ for $a\in \R$ are compact.

Fix a matrix $X\in \R_{\ge 0}^{p \times N}$. Let $(\param_{n})_{n\ge 0}$, $\param_{n}:=(W_{n}, H_{n})$ be generated by \eqref{eq:MUPR_NMF} with arbitrary initialization $\param_{0}\in \Param:=\R_{\ge 0}^{p\times r}\times \R_{\ge 0}^{r\times N}$. Denote $f(W,H):=\frac{1}{2}\lVert X- WH \rVert_{F}^{2}$.

Let $\param_{n}:=[U^{(1)}_{n},\dots,U^{(m)}_{n}]$, $n\ge 0$ be generated by \eqref{eq:BMM_DR_CTF} with one of the options \ref{eq:ALS_DR_CTF}, \ref{eq:ALS_PR_CTF}, \ref{eq:ALS_DR_PR_CTF} (for general convex constraints on factor matrices) or \ref{eq:MUR_NCPD} (for NCPD).  Then \textbf{\textup{(i)}}-\textbf{\textup{(iii)}} of Theorem \ref{thm:complexity} holds for $(\param_{n})_{n\ge 0}$.

issues.failure_explanation: Assumption A2 requires that the sublevel sets of the objective function $f$ on $\Param$ are compact. However, for the NMF objective $f(W,H) = \frac{1}{2}\|X - WH\|_F^2$ on $\Param = \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}^{p\times r} \times \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}^{r\times N}$ (and similarly for unconstrained or nonnegatively constrained tensor CP-decomposition in Corollary 5.2), there is an inherent scaling invariance: for any $c > 0$ and any diagonal scaling $D$, $f(W D, D^{-1} H) = f(W, H)$. Thus, every non-empty sublevel set containing a non-zero point contains unbounded rays and is therefore non-compact. Because A2 fails, Proposition 3.3 (boundedness of iterates) and all downstream uniform Lipschitz gradient bounds do not hold without compactness constraints.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the domain of the factor matrices in NMF and CTF to compact convex subsets (e.g., imposing an explicit upper bound on the Frobenius or spectral norm of factor matrices), or prove iterate boundedness directly from the properties of the regularized algorithms without relying on compactness of sublevel sets.
issues.overall_effect: Corollaries 5.1 and 5.2 as stated are unsupported because the main theorem (Theorem 2.1) requires Assumption A2, which is violated by the matrix and tensor factorization formulations.
issues.title: Sublevel sets of matrix and tensor factorization objectives violate compactness assumption A2
issues.why_classification: Imposing bounded convex constraint sets (e.g., norm bounds) on the factors is a standard adjustment in constrained matrix/tensor factorization that preserves the convergence and complexity statements without altering the overarching proof architecture of Theorem 2.1.

issues.failure_explanation: In the proof of Corollary 5.1, the surrogate $g_n^j$ is defined by Taylor expansion around $\mathbf{h}_n = H_n^j$. The true gradient of this surrogate is $\nabla g_n^j(H^j) = -W_n^T X^j + W_n^T W_n H_n^j + (\mathbf{D}_n^j + \rho \mathbf{I})(H^j - H_n^j)$. In (40), the author replaces $H_n^j$ with $\tilde{H}_n^j = H_n^j \lor \delta$ without justification. Because $\mathbf{D}_n^j \tilde{H}_n^j = W_n^T W_n \tilde{H}_n^j$, the terms cancel at $\tilde{H}_n^j$, but they do not cancel at $H_n^j$ whenever any coordinate of $H_n^j$ is below $\delta$. Hence $H_{n+1}^j$ in (34) is not the minimizer of $g_n^j$. If instead $g_n^j$ were defined by expanding around $\tilde{H}_n^j$, then $g_n^j(H_n^j) \ne f_n^j(H_n^j)$, which violates the sharpness requirement $g_n(H_n) = f_n(H_n)$ of BMM. Consequently, MUR cannot be represented as an exact BMM instance with surrogate (36).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Redefine the surrogate function so that it both satisfies the sharpness condition at $H_n$ and has an exact nonnegative minimizer matching (34), or explicitly account for the discrepancy $g_n(H_{n+1}) - g_n(H_{n+1}^\star)$ as an inexact update gap satisfying Assumption A4.
issues.overall_effect: The proof that the MUR algorithm (34) for NMF (and option (f) in Corollary 5.2 for NCPD) fits into the BMM framework and therefore inherits the rate and stationarity guarantees of Theorem 2.1 is invalid.
issues.title: MUR update does not minimize the specified majorizing surrogate
issues.why_classification: The failure affects the verification that MUR is a valid BMM algorithm. A contained revision of the surrogate definition or an analysis treating the thresholding as an inexact subproblem update can restore the connection to BMM without changing the algorithm or overarching proof architecture.
